description: We are a team of second-year Engineering students,new to hackathons and excited to learn. We are working on "Abandoned but not Forgotten" and want to tell the story of NASA'S equipment left on the Moon and Mars.
summary:
Ghost Rovers: Left Behind, Still Speaking by Team Pixel Pulsar is an interactive web experience built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge (“Abandoned but not forgotten”). Designed for explorers aged 10–14, it brings five historic lunar and Martian machines (Eagle, Lunar Laser Reflectors, Apollo 15 Buggy, Opportunity, and Ingenuity) to life through first-person storytelling, interactive mini-simulations, and a ghost collection radar.
The project addresses the challenge by transforming resting hardware into relatable, educational storytellers. It is important because it connects the next generation to space heritage and verified NASA science—proving that off-world artifacts are not forgotten relics, but enduring monuments to human curiosity that paved the way for future exploration.
details:
What it does: Ghost Rovers is a gamified mission-control web app where kids act as space detectives and “wake” five machines NASA left on the Moon and Mars: Eagle, the Lunar Laser Reflectors, the Apollo 15 Moon Buggy, Opportunity and Ingenuity. Each one tells its own story in first person through a retro typewriter interface. Each also has a mini-simulation tied to a real number, such as the 3.8 cm/year lunar drift or Ingenuity’s 2,400 RPM rotors. After waking all five, players take a 3-question quiz and unlock a printable “Junior Space Explorer” certificate.

Benefits and impact: It turns “space junk” into living history for kids aged 10-14, using hands-on play instead of a textbook. Every fact comes from official NASA sources, and it’s free, works on a phone or a classroom computer, and needs no install. We hope it sparks interest in STEM and planetary science.

Tools: HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript with no frameworks or dependencies. The Web Audio API makes the sound effects live, with no MP3 files. It is hosted on Netlify, and the data comes from NASA NSSDCA, ILRS, NASA Science and the NASA Image and Video Library.

Creativity: Instead of describing abandoned hardware, we let the hardware speak for itself. Kids learn by playing detective, not by reading.

Factors considered: Accuracy (no invented facts), an age-appropriate design for 10-14, accessibility (tested down to 360px, high contrast, reduced-motion support), and fast loading on any device.
